subject: Promo credit triage - FastFlow suspicious cluster
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Promo credit triage - FastFlow suspicious cluster

Team —

I ran the self-serve credit issuance audit run this morning and flagged a cluster of signups tied to the FastFlow acquisition campaign. Quick summary: 42 accounts created between 2026-11-24 22:00 and 2026-11-25 03:10 UTC; 36 of them received the standard $250 trial credit automatically.

Indicators:
- Many emails use short-lived domains (examples in attached CSV).
- IPs resolve to the same /24 range with very low diversity (see ip-heatmap).
- Two accounts used the same phone verification token (possible reuse).

Given the scale and the consistent patterns, I recommend pausing further auto-grants for signups that match these signals and doing targeted reversals for the 36 grants pending manual review.

Requesting:
1) Approve temporary hold on auto-credits for signups where domain matches *.lighthouse[0-9]{2}.tk OR where IP risk score > 0.8.
2) Approve reversal for the 36 grants until we confirm legitimacy.
3) If we need to reach out to the buyer/partner (FastFlow), who should own outreach? CS or Sales?

Attachments: signup-export-fastflow-1125.csv (sample rows), ip-heatmap-fastflow-1125.png, hs-case-2345.pdf (precreated HubSpot case).

Karthik
Director, Growth Ops
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Promo credit triage - FastFlow suspicious cluster

Thanks Karthik —

Hold makes sense. Please flip the auto-grant flag for the FastFlow campaign immediately. For reversals: start with accounts that match all three signals (disposable domain + same /24 IP + reused phone token). Keep the rest flagged for manual outreach.

On outreach ownership: Sales should try a short-clarifying message first ("did you run a recruitment/hackathon?") — if there’s pushback or evidence of abuse, CS escalates and we proceed with reversals.

Also add a note to the HubSpot case mentioning we’ve paused new grants and expect 24–48h for the manual review.

- Dev

I’m Rajiv from platform ops at FastFlow. We saw a notification that a number of our signups were flagged. We ran an internal event (hackweek) across teams in APAC last week; many participants used short-lived test addresses and a mobile test-bench that routes via a shared proxy. 

I’ve attached a short internal log (ops+lighthouse@fastflow.ai) that shows the event timestamps and signed-off attendees. Can you share the account emails you plan to reverse so we can confirm legitimacy? We’d like to avoid reversing legitimate test accounts.

Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick response and the context. We want to be careful here. To balance risk vs. customer experience we propose this path: 

1) We will hold reversals for accounts that you confirm are tied to your internal event. Please provide a list of the attendee emails and any event token you used.
2) For the remaining accounts that you do not confirm within 48 hours, we will reverse credits and block further free-grants matching the patterns noted earlier.
3) We will provide you with a CSV of the 36 accounts we plan to reverse by 2026-11-28 18:00 UTC.

If you can share the attendee list and the event token by EOD UTC, we’ll exclude those from reversal. We’ll note the hold in HubSpot case HS-2345 and keep this thread for audit.
